title: strange behaviour with remapped Win+C → Win+V
author: luxferre
summary: On Windows 11, remapping Win+C to Win+V opens Clipboard History but releasing Win immediately dismisses the surface.
next_action: Reproduce on current Windows 11 and trace injected versus physical modifier key-up ordering.

confidence.rationale: The exact release sequence was independently reproduced by a maintainer.

judgment.rationale: A maintainer reproduced the exact key-up behavior and distinguished it from the older Win+V failure report.
evidence: The issue gives a four-step remap and focus sequence.
The reporter confirms native Win+V stays open while remapped Win+C closes on Win release.
A maintainer reproduced the dismissal specifically when the Win key-up is delivered after C is released.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on current Windows 11 and trace injected versus physical modifier key-up ordering.

fix_assessment.rationale: The failure is reproducible, but the current injected/physical key event sequence must be captured before selecting a state-machine change.

issue_context.summary: On Windows 11, remapping Win+C to Win+V opens Clipboard History but releasing Win immediately dismisses the surface.
known_information: The original affected version is PowerToys 0.59.1.
The symptom occurs on Windows 11 but not Windows 10 in the original report.
inferences: The shell surface may observe a physical Win key-up after the remapped Win+V sequence and treat it as dismissal input.
issue_context.analysis: A current low-level key sequence trace can determine whether Keyboard Manager should suppress, reorder, or synthesize modifier release for this shell shortcut.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and all maintainer comments.
Confirmed #14556 is a different Win+V failure rather than the remap-specific dismissal sequence.

actions.label: Reproduce Win+C to Win+V dismissal
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Trace modifier release for a remapped shell shortcut
setup: Create a shortcut remap from Win+C to Win+V.
steps: Press Win+C and confirm Clipboard History opens.
Release C while continuing to hold Win and observe the surface.
Release Win and record whether the surface closes.
Compare with native Win+V and capture Keyboard Manager key-event logging for both sequences.
reproduce.expected_result: The remapped shortcut leaves Clipboard History open after Win is released, matching native Win+V.
